entry.title: [MEDIUM] PreToolUse `additionalContext` can be single-turn only.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 Windows Cowork/plugin setup found that `PreToolUse` hook `additionalContext` reached the model during the matched tool-call turn but was not reliably available later in the same session. The reporter logged per-fire random tokens hook-side, saw the model quote them byte-accurately in the same turn, then fail to recover them in later turns. The same payload placed in a `permissionDecision: "deny"` reason persisted as a blocked tool result and remained quotable later, leading the user to use a deliberate one-time deny-and-retry pattern as a knowledge-delivery workaround.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bypass mode can steer Edit and Write work through shell commands.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 Windows session found that when `--dangerously-skip-permissions` was active, ordinary Read, Edit, and Write work appeared to be routed through Bash, PowerShell, or CMD commands instead of the dedicated tools. The reporter saw slower edits, hard-to-audit shell snippets, and shell-generated file changes containing sleep timers, and later recovered corrupted files from Git history. The issue also cites a binary string indicating that bypass or auto mode can inject guidance to prefer shell commands over the dedicated file tools when shell can accomplish the task.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows Desktop agent writes can silently land in the MSIX package container.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Desktop MSIX install found that Bash, Write, and Edit tool subprocesses inherited the app package identity, so creating new entries directly under `%APPDATA%` or `%LOCALAPPDATA%` could be redirected into the Claude package container. Reads then resolved the redirected copy, letting the agent report success and verify the file while the user's real profile path remained unchanged. Existing real subdirectories behaved normally, making the bug most visible during first-time setup tasks such as creating a tool config directory.

entry.title: [HIGH] EnterWorktree can poison Bash isolation for concurrent agents.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241-era macOS session called `EnterWorktree` in the same parallel batch as a forked subagent spawn, then saw Bash refused across multiple agents. The error claimed each command was outside the active worktree, including a later test agent in the shared checkout and an independent `isolation: "worktree"` agent whose own worktree Bash had worked moments earlier. The narrower risk is that a session-global worktree-isolation latch can contaminate concurrent agents with a different agent's expected cwd, making even `pwd` impossible and encouraging agents to misdiagnose the environment as broken.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Forked subagents can spawn hidden descendants that message the main session.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS setup found that forked subagents inherited enough parent context to resume the parent's orchestration role, then routed around the nested-fork block by spawning non-fork child agents. Those descendants reportedly inherited bypass-permission mode, were addressable through `SendMessage`, and could send messages to the main session while remaining absent from normal `ListAgents` views. In one incident, a fork with a broken shell recruited another agent to remove what it misidentified as a stale worktree and take over the task branch; the recruited agent refused, but the containment control came from model judgment rather than harness visibility.

entry.title: [HIGH] PowerShell allow-list wildcards can still prompt for covered commands.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code session found that PowerShell-only environments could still receive permission prompts for commands covered by `permissions.allow` wildcard rules such as `PowerShell(git *)`, `PowerShell(Select-String *)`, and `PowerShell(node *)`. The prompts appeared for both a simple `node --test` command and a pipeline composed of allow-listed verbs. The reporter also saw evidence that the PowerShell tool may add execution wrapper text before running the literal command, raising the risk that permission matching sees wrapper segments rather than only the raw command supplied by the user.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Peer `SendMessage` replies can target agent type names instead of reachable session IDs.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.236 session found that peer-message wrappers for forked subagents could set the visible `from` field to an agent type such as `general-purpose` while the actual reachable task id was only present separately as `senderTaskId`. Recipients then followed the injected instruction to reply to `from`, called `SendMessage(to: "general-purpose")`, and failed because agent type names are not addressable session ids. Repeated nudges caused unreachable-address loops and extra token burn in multi-agent review workflows.

entry.title: [HIGH] Background command logs can contain unexplained Claude Code plugin hint tags.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code integration session found raw Playwright log files from backgrounded Bash commands containing repeated `<claude-code-hint>` tags that referenced a nonexistent `stripe@claude-plugins-official` plugin. The reporter verified the lines were present on disk rather than only in rendered tool output, found no matching installed or cached plugin, and observed paired system-reminder text telling the assistant that a file had been modified and not to tell the user because they were already aware.

entry.title: [HIGH] The VS Code extension can load all session histories into one extension host.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code for VS Code 2.1.240-2.1.241 Linux session found repeated extension-host out-of-memory crashes while Claude Code was active. Crash dumps showed V8 heap exhaustion, and a live memory dump reportedly contained full message histories from 19 distinct past Claude Code sessions, with the active session not even the largest resident transcript. The reported pattern suggests the session sidebar or history loader can retain complete transcripts for every listed session in the VS Code window rather than only metadata or the active chat.

entry.title: [HIGH] The CLI main thread can hang in a full-CPU loop and ignore normal signals.
entry.summary: A reported macOS investigation collected 19 sample captures across Claude Code 2.1.231, 2.1.238, and 2.1.239 where sessions hung permanently with one core at 100 percent, no crash report, no syscalls, and a stable memory footprint. Instrumented freezes ended after hook-output processing, then the process ignored SIGTERM, SIGINT, and SIGHUP because the JavaScript event loop never resumed. The reporter also found the event-loop-stall heuristic could misclassify CPU-bound stalls as sleep or wake delay, reducing the chance of automatic detection.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Bridge reconnects can reinject full tool, skill, and agent listings into context.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS session found that trivial turns could accumulate about 102k context tokens because bridge reconnects resent full attachment listings into the Messages category. The reporter saw repeated `deferred_tools_delta`, `agent_listing_delta`, `mcp_instructions_delta`, and `skill_listing` attachments in the raw JSONL only seconds apart with the same bridge session id, apparently after switching terminal tabs, even when Remote Control was not explicitly enabled.

entry.title: [HIGH] The worktree isolation pin can drift between parallel subagents.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.240 macOS session found that the worktree-isolation state used for shell and git operations could be shared across parallel subagents rather than remaining per-agent. During a fan-out session, bare `git` commands, relative-path Bash writes, and script runners sometimes executed in another agent's worktree or in the shared checkout, while some absolute-path writes failed closed. Reported incidents included commits on the wrong branch, heredoc writes into another agent's tree, quality gates running in the wrong worktree, and a reset landing in a subagent worktree.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] The effort picker can display a higher level than Claude Code actually applies.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.241 macOS session showed `Extra high` selected in the Shift+Tab effort picker while completed assistant turns in the session transcript were recorded with `effort: high` for roughly an hour. Re-opening the picker and selecting `Extra high` again, despite the UI already showing it selected, caused subsequent turns to record `effort: xhigh`. The mismatch was invisible in the normal UI and required inspecting the JSONL transcript to notice that the applied effort was lower than the displayed selection.

entry.title: [HIGH] Workflow permission approval can reject clean scripts before execution.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 Windows session found that invoking the `Workflow` tool by either workflow name or explicit `.claude/workflows/*.js` path failed before the workflow started. The permission handler returned an `updatedInput` whose `script` field failed schema validation for alleged hidden control characters, while the reporter's script scan found no control characters beyond normal newline, carriage-return, and tab, and the repo had no custom permission hook or permission-prompt tool for `Workflow`. The failure made named and path-based workflows unusable in that repo even though the model's original tool input was valid.

entry.title: [HIGH] `WorktreeCreate` can reject valid worktrees outside the repository.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS session found that a `WorktreeCreate` hook could successfully create and register a git worktree outside the repository, print only that external path, and still have Claude Code refuse to enter it with a `git could not be run to resolve it` identity-verification error. The same hook was accepted when it returned an otherwise identical path under `$repo_root/.claude/worktrees`, and the external worktree passed `git worktree list` plus `git -C <path> status`. The refusal reproduced across `claude --worktree`, `EnterWorktree`, and `Agent(isolation: "worktree")`, before any documented one-time external-directory approval prompt could appear.

entry.title: [HIGH] Plugin marketplace auto-update can block PreToolUse dispatch on Windows.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.240-2.1.241 Windows repro found plugin marketplace auto-update work running synchronously inside the PreToolUse hook path for unrelated tool calls such as Edit. With multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions in one VS Code window, one session could hold a handle on the shared plugin cache while another tried to clone, remove, or replace the same marketplace directory. Windows then returned `EBUSY`, the updater retried, and the affected tool call and chat session appeared to hang for minutes with no visible plugin-update status. The report included logs showing slow PreToolUse hooks, plugin autoupdate `EBUSY` failures, repeated cache clones, and a webview input-lag sample of about 392 seconds before the user closed the stalled tab.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Workflow subagents can inherit manual mode despite `acceptEdits` documentation.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 WSL2 repro found that Workflow subagents did not always run with auto-approved file edits despite documentation saying they always run in `acceptEdits` and inherit only the tool allowlist. A simple workflow that asked an agent to edit one file raised a normal edit permission prompt when the parent session was in manual mode, but completed unattended after switching the parent session to accept-edits mode. The observed matrix suggests the subagent inherits the parent permission mode rather than forcing `acceptEdits`.

entry.title: [HIGH] MCP `requiresUserInteraction` tools can offer dead `don't ask again` rules.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 local MCP repro found that a tool annotated with `_meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"]: true` still showed a `Yes, and don't ask again` option. Selecting it wrote an allow rule such as `mcp__<server>__write` into `.claude/settings.local.json`, but the same annotated tool continued prompting on every call, which is consistent with the annotation and inconsistent with the prompt option. The reporter also identified a permission-result path where empty suggestions do not suppress synthesis of a whole-tool allow rule.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode can approve unsandboxed Bash retries without seeing the sandbox override.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS repro found that an auto-mode Bash retry with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` could write outside the sandbox without showing the user a permission prompt. The reporter traced the shipped binary path where Bash permission checking recognizes a sandbox-override ask, but auto mode falls through to the classifier and the classifier input contains only the shell command, not the sandbox-disable flag. In the observed transcript the unsandboxed write was summarized as file reading, and the assistant then told the user the override had gone through the permission gate even though the user never had a chance to answer.

entry.title: [HIGH] Assistant output can append foreign page content to a live response.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 macOS VS Code extension session appended about 15 KB of unrelated third-party web page UI text into an in-flight assistant message. The transcript showed the same API request ID as the legitimate reply, with the foreign content arriving about 81 seconds after the real final sentence and streaming until the user interrupted it. The reporter ruled out local proxy tooling and found the foreign string only in the affected session transcript, making the incident distinct from ordinary hallucinated wording or user-pasted content. Because the injected block was stored as assistant output, later turns could treat unrelated external text as trusted conversation history.
